summary: Charge the model for big weights and the wiggles calm down.
headline: A price on wild curves
overview: Ridge regression adds the squared size of the weights to the loss. A flexible curve can still fit, but only if it pays for steep swings.
Turn the penalty up from nothing and watch the degree-9 curve settle. Turn it too far and it goes flat.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Keep turning the penalty up. Past a point the curve flattens and both errors rise: that is underfitting.

check.question: What happens if the penalty is made enormous?
options: The model fits the training data perfectly
The weights shrink toward zero and the model underfits

realLife: Almost every production linear model has a penalty, tuned with cross-validation.
data: The same fourteen points as the overfitting lesson, with degree 9 as the starting point. Penalty strengths run from off to 1e0 in decades.
maths: ridge loss = Σ (ŷ − y)² + α Σ w²
lasso loss = (1/2n) Σ (ŷ − y)² + α Σ |w|  (can set weights exactly to zero)
scikit-learn's Ridge uses a summed error, so its α is not the same size as a penalty added to a mean error. Compare the formulas before comparing numbers across sources.
code:
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
m = make_pipeline(PolynomialFeatures(9), StandardScaler(), Ridge(alpha=0.1))
